item.text: {"text":"Replacement histories need plausibility controls: preserve sequence length, timestamps/order, padding and replacement positions; vary only a small, reported number of interactions. Learning Causal Explanations for Recommendation uses fixed-length replacements sampled from a learned history distribution, while CETD emphasizes temporal dependencies and proximity to the original history. Neighborhood-based perturbations also appear in substitution-attack defenses. These support comparing uniform replacements against locally plausible replacements matched on training-item frequency and semantic or transition similarity, using only available training histories and metadata. Report replacement count, recency and plausibility separately; unrealistic-history sensitivity alone does not establish useful context dependence. Sources: [Learning Causal Explanations](https://csr21.github.io/xu-csr2021.pdf), [CETD](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/20/11176), [Substitution-Based Profile Pollution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.11237).\n\nRecommended diagnostic synthesis: freeze the model, original target, candidate identities, candidate order and eligibility mask across paired original/perturbed histories. Never resample negatives or recompute seen-item exclusions after replacement: either changes the ranking problem. For a clean context-only probe, choose replacements outside the frozen candidates and exclude the held-out target. Measure original-target score change, rank change and target-versus-fixed-negative margin changes. Separately run a candidate-overlap probe and report inserted-item score/rank gains; recompute diagnostic target ranks after identically removing inserted candidates from both conditions. Disappearing rank effects indicate direct candidate competition; persistent target-score or margin changes indicate broader context sensitivity. Use identity replacements and matched random replacements as controls, with paired uncertainty estimates. Keep these auxiliary diagnostics separate from the pinned benchmark, whose candidates and evaluator must remain unchanged. This decomposition is an experimental recommendation, not a demonstrated causal identification result."}
